Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 37, verse 18–29 (part 1 of 4):

The student: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ ﴿It will be but a single shout, and at once they will be looking on.﴾ ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense!"﴾ ﴿"This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny."﴾ ﴿"Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship,﴾ ﴿"besides Allah, and guide them to the path of Hellfire.﴾ ﴿"And stop them, for they are to be questioned."﴾ ﴿"What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?"﴾ ﴿"Nay, but this day they will submit."﴾ [As-Saffat 18–26].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again? And our forefathers of old?"﴾. This interrogation, Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to answer with His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes"﴾, meaning: you will be resurrected. And ﴿نَعَمْ (na'am)﴾ (yes) is the particle of answer used to affirm something positively as confirmation, and it is likewise used to answer a negative for confirmation. So it is a particle of answer for confirmation, whether the statement is negative or affirmative. If you say, "Did Zayd stand up?" you say, "Na'am" to confirm it. And you say, "La" (no) to deny it, meaning to negate it.
As for (bala) (on the contrary/yes), it is the particle of answer used only to answer a negative. Is it for confirming it or for denying it? It is for denying it. If someone says, "Did Zayd not stand up?" the answer is "Bala" (yes indeed).
We said that (na'am) is used to answer both negation and affirmation for confirmation, meaning: to affirm what follows the interrogative hamza. "Did Zayd stand up?" Fine. "Did Zayd not stand up?" "Na'am," meaning, he did not stand up. (Bala) is used to answer only a negation and does not come with an affirmation, but to deny it, not to confirm it. So if you say, "Did Zayd not stand up?" the answer is "Bala," meaning he has indeed stood up, contrary to what you negated; and the phrase "he has stood up" contradicts "he did not stand up," so it is in fact a denial. As for (la) (no), it is a particle of answer used only with an affirmation, to deny it: is it to deny it or to confirm it? To deny it. "Did Zayd stand up?" If you say "La," it means he did not stand up.
So these are the three particles of answer. Which is the most general? (Na'am), because it occurs with affirmation and it occurs with negation; whereas (bala) and (la) are each specific to something: (bala) to negation, and (la) to affirmation.
Fine, let us now look at the noble verse: ﴿Say, "Yes"﴾, this is for confirmation, meaning: yes, you will be resurrected.
For this reason the author estimated that in his saying "(tub'athun)" (you will be resurrected), meaning: you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection after having been dust and bones; but you will not be resurrected as you were in the world, in might and luxury, but rather ﴿and you will be humbled﴾, i.e. abased. The clause here is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of the omitted verb which is inferred from the answer, or from the deputy subject of the verb estimated after the answer. Yes, "you will be resurrected while you are humbled." Al-Dukhur means abasement and humiliation; meaning: they will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection in a state of abasement, not as they were in the world, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you will see them exposed to it, humbled by abasement, looking with a furtive glance﴾ [Ash-Shura 45]. Whereas in the world one of them used to turn his eyeballs as he wished, in the Hereafter they look with a furtive glance full of shame, disgrace and dishonour, and we seek refuge with Allah. (You will be resurrected ﴿while you are humbled﴾).
﴿It will be but a single shout, and at once they will be looking on.﴾ Meaning: if the matter is so, that they will be resurrected, is there need for treatment and for a period of time? The answer is no. ﴿It will be﴾, i.e. their being roused for resurrection, ﴿but a single shout﴾. This is the most correct view regarding the referent of the pronoun; for this reason the author said: (a vague pronoun explained by ﴿shout﴾). So "hiya" is a pronoun whose referent is derived from the predicate; i.e., it is but a single shout for their resurrection.
What the author estimated as the referent of the pronoun is the correct view; so the referent of the pronoun is the predicate. Some of them said: ﴿It will be﴾, i.e. the resurrection which they will undergo, meaning: their resurrection will be nothing but a single shout, i.e. by a single shout. But what the author estimated is preferable. ﴿It will be but a single shout﴾. The author said: (i.e. a cry) by which they are roused, and it is said: "Come out" — meaning from the graves. When it is said, "Come out from the graves," they come out as one man, none of them left behind. Do they come out slowly? The answer is no, because of Allah's saying: ﴿And Our command is but a single act, like a glance of the eye﴾ [Al-Qamar 50]. So the matter does not need repeated demands to come out, nor a respite in time; rather, as soon as it is said, "Come out," ﴿at once they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. This is part of the perfection of the power of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.
(﴿It will be but a single shout﴾, i.e. one cry by which they are roused, ﴿and at once﴾, i.e. the creatures are alive, ﴿they will be looking on﴾ at what is done to them). The fa' is a conjunctive particle, and (idha) is the sudden-occurrence (fuja'iyya) particle, i.e. in the moment there is a sudden surprise: they are looking on. The grammarians differed regarding idha al-fuja'iyya: is it a particle, so that it has no place in grammatical analysis, or is it an adverb? We are not concerned to estimate it as a particle or as an adverb; what matters is that we know its meaning, which is that it indicates suddenness; meaning, it comes quickly.
His saying: ﴿and at once they will be looking on﴾ indicates that as soon as they come out, they will be living and perceiving, and they are not like the infant who comes out of its mother's womb knowing nothing. In the world people come out of their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, but after that Allah gives them hearing, sight and hearts: hearing by which they hear and understand, and sight likewise by which they see and understand. For this reason you find that the child, as soon as he is born, does not turn to anything; a lamp passes before him at its brightest and he does not know what it is; then gradually he begins to recognise colours when they vary before him, and follows with his eyes. But those who are raised from the graves are not made to wait in this manner; that is, their hearing, sight and hearts do not grow gradually, but as soon as they come out, ﴿at once they are looking on﴾.
The author said: (﴿at once﴾, i.e. the creatures are alive, looking on at what is done to them). If someone says: the author said "i.e. the creatures," although the context of the verses requires that what is meant is these deniers and their forefathers: ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again? And our forefathers of old?"﴾. If we take the context, we say the pronoun refers to these people and their forefathers; if we look at the reality, we say the pronoun refers to all creatures, and the reality is that all creatures come out with this shout: ﴿at once they are looking on﴾.
The author informed us by his saying (at what is done to them) that the looking here is looking with the eye, not in the sense of waiting; although the verse may admit that the meaning is looking with the eye, or waiting. Looking comes in the sense of waiting, as in Allah's saying: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾ [Muhammad 18], where "yanzurun" means "yantazirun" (they wait).
﴿at once they will be looking on﴾ (﴿And they will say﴾, i.e. the disbelievers; ﴿ya﴾ is for alerting; ﴿waylana﴾ our destruction, and it is a verbal noun with no verb from its own root; and the angels will say to them: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾).
﴿And they will say﴾: he used the past tense although the saying is future, to establish that it will certainly occur; this is common in the Arabic language and the Noble Qur'an, that the future is expressed by the past to establish its occurrence. An example is Allah's saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾, for the command of Allah has not yet come, as is shown by His saying: ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl 1]; but ﴿has come﴾ here means "will come," and the future is expressed by the past to establish its occurrence.
So His saying here: ﴿And they said﴾ means "and they will say," but He expressed it with the past for the certainty of its occurrence. His saying "i.e. the disbelievers" is accurate; yet if he had said "﴿And they said﴾, i.e. those who denied the resurrection, who said ﴿'When we have died...'﴾", it would have been more precise in the commentary, because the disbeliever is more general than the one who denies the resurrection; is that not so? He may disbelieve without denying the resurrection; but the matter admits some leniency in expression.
As for His saying: ﴿"Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense"﴾, the author said that ﴿ya﴾ is for alerting, and that wayl is a verbal noun for an omitted verb estimated from its meaning, not from its wording. But it may be that ﴿ya﴾ is a vocative particle, and that they called upon "woe," as if they said: "O woe to us, appear! This is your time." Wayl here means intense regret and also punishment; Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ [Al-Mursalat 15], meaning regret and punishment. So here ﴿O woe to us﴾ means: O our regret, O our punishment, appear, for this is your time. And it may, as the author said, be that ﴿ya﴾ is for alerting.
But if someone says: does (ya) come for alerting? The answer is yes. If we are asked for an example that admits only alerting, we say: like Allah's saying: ﴿"O would that my people knew"﴾ [Ya-Sin 26], where (ya) is for alerting, because (ya) does not enter upon particles but upon nouns; it is brought here for alerting.
His saying: ﴿waylana﴾ means "our destruction"; but wayl, as I said, is more specific than mere destruction; rather it is regret and punishment. (It is a verbal noun), meaning wayl is a verbal noun (with no verb from its own wording), but from its meaning. If it is from its meaning and we interpret wayl as destruction, how do we estimate the verb? ("we were destroyed, our destruction")? Like that?
﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾: the author said: (and the angels will say to them: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾), so the commentator, may Allah have mercy on him, made ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾ the speech of the angels.
﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ [Al-Mursalat 15], i.e. regret and punishment, so here ﴿O woe to us﴾ [As-Saffat 20], i.e. O our regret and O our punishment, appear, for this is your time. It may, as the author said, be that (ya) is for alerting. But if someone says: does (ya) come for alerting? The answer is yes; if we are asked for an example that admits only alerting, we say: like Allah's saying: ﴿"O would that my people knew"﴾ [Ya-Sin 26], where (ya) is for alerting, because (ya) does not enter upon particles but upon nouns; it is brought here for alerting.
His saying: ﴿waylana﴾ [As-Saffat 20] (our destruction). But wayl, as I said, is more specific than mere destruction; rather it is regret and punishment. (It is a verbal noun), meaning it is a verbal noun (with no verb from its own wording), but from its meaning. If it is from its meaning and we interpret wayl as destruction, how do we estimate the verb? "We were destroyed, our destruction," O our destruction, our destruction.
﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾ [As-Saffat 20]: the author said: (and the angels say to them: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾).
The author, or the commentator, made ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾ the speech of the angels; but the correct view is that it is their speech, i.e. the speech of these deniers, meaning that on that day they acknowledge the Day of Recompense, but acknowledgement will not benefit them then. They acknowledge this day when they witness it, saying: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾, and the one indicated is the time in which they are, that present day. "Al-Din" means the reward; and know that "al-din" is applied to recompense and sometimes applied to deeds: Allah's saying ﴿"For you is your religion, and for me is my religion"﴾ [Al-Kafirun 6] means deeds.
His saying the Exalted: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? The day when no soul will possess anything for another soul﴾ [Al-Infitar 17–19], the meaning of "din" is recompense.
And here ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾ [As-Saffat 20] means recompense, i.e. this is the Day of Recompense; and as "din" is applied to recompense it is applied to deeds, as I said, and from it the saying: "As you do, so you will be repaid" (kama tadin tudan), i.e. as you act, so you will be recompensed.
He said: (﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾, i.e. the reckoning and recompense; ﴿This is the Day of Separation﴾ between the creatures; ﴿which you used to deny﴾ [As-Saffat 21]). This sentence may be from their speech, or it may be from the speech of the angels. If it is from their speech, the meaning is that some of them say to others: ﴿This is the Day of Separation which you used to deny﴾ [As-Saffat 21].
Some of them say to others this as rebuke, reproach and condemnation; and if it is from the speech of the angels there is no difficulty, for they address a people who denied it.
His saying: ﴿This is the Day of Separation﴾ [As-Saffat 21], after ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾, because when people are repaid, reckoned and requited, they separate: some of them separate from others, a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. A man may be separated from his father, from his mother, from his relatives: these to Paradise and those to the Fire. Thus it is called the Day of Separation because creatures are separated on it, some turned to the Fire and some turned to Paradise.
It is also called the Day of Separation because creatures are separated on it by judgement among them, by taking the right of the wronged from the wrongdoer, as the judge in the world separates between litigants, giving the wronged his right from the wrongdoer. It is called the Day of Separation because people separate from one another: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze; and it is called the Day of Separation because it separates the creatures by judging among them with justice.
His saying: ﴿which you used to deny﴾ [As-Saffat 21]: ﴿you used to﴾ refers to the past; now they acknowledge it, for they said: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾; but in the past they denied this day and said: how can creatures be raised after they were bones and dust?
﴿This is the Day of Separation which you used to deny﴾. If someone says: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿which you used to deny﴾?
We say: the benefit is to increase the regret of these people; for when it is said to them, "that which you used to deny," they will regret and say: "Would that we had not denied," so there will be additional pain in their souls. That is one aspect.
Another aspect: reproach of these people and blame for their denial, since they denied the truth. So there are two benefits:
The first benefit: increasing their regret.
The second benefit: reproach and blame for their denial of the truth. ﴿This is the Day of Separation which you used to deny﴾.
(And it is said to the angels: ﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾ by associating partners with themselves, ﴿and their spouses﴾, their companions from the devils, ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, i.e. other than Him, of idols; ﴿then guide them﴾, show them and drive them ﴿to the path of Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat 22–23], the road to the Fire). We seek refuge with Allah!
﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾: the address here is from Allah, and Allah knows best, to the angels; and "ihshuru" means gather together, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Mutual Loss﴾ [At-Taghabun 9]. It is called the Day of Gathering and the Day of Assembly because people are assembled and gathered on it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 37, verses 18–29 (part 2 of 4):

And His saying: ﴿Those who did wrong﴾ (to themselves, through shirk). It should be said: those who wronged themselves and wronged others, because Allah, glorified and exalted is He, omitted the object. What does the omission of the object indicate? Generality. So in reality they wronged themselves and wronged others, especially their leaders who led their followers astray, for they wronged them by mixing truth with falsehood and misguiding them.

﴿Those who did wrong and their spouses﴾. The author said: (their companions from the devils). Every spouse (zawj) is a companion (qarin), and this includes a husband and his wife, for they are companions. It was also said that the intended meaning of "spouses" (azwaj) is kinds and types, and from this is His saying: ﴿and other [punishments] of similar kinds﴾ [Sad 58], meaning types. The meanings are close, because generally the companion is of the same kind as the one he accompanies. This is as came in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A man is upon the religion of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he takes as a close friend." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (4833) and al-Tirmidhi (2378), from Abu Hurayrah.]

﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾. That is: and what they used to worship. When? In the world. For this reason the past tense verb was used: ﴿they used to worship﴾, meaning in the world. The clause ﴿they used to worship﴾ is the relative clause (silat al-mawsul) of the relative pronoun, and the returning pronoun (a'id) is omitted, and its estimated form is: and what they used to worship besides Allah.

As for the author's saying: (from the idols). If someone asks: how can idols be gathered when they are inanimate objects, upon whom there is no reckoning or punishment? The answer is that they are gathered to the Fire and thrown into it as a humiliation for their worshippers. As for the idols themselves, they have no awareness; they feel neither humiliation nor honor. But their worshippers are the ones who feel humiliation when their objects of worship are thrown into the Fire. So these objects of worship are thrown into the Fire as a humiliation for their worshippers, and as a demonstration that they cannot benefit them at the time when they most need their benefit.

And His saying: ﴿and what they used to worship (22) besides Allah﴾. This verse is general, and it was specified by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya 101]. For if we took it in its full generality, there would be people who worship the prophets, and people who worship the angels. Would these objects of worship then be gathered with these worshippers?

The answer is no: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will [all] arrive at it﴾ [al-Anbiya 98].

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾. Accordingly, the generality here is specified by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾.

It was also said that the generality remains as it is, but it is a general expression by which a specific meaning is intended. It intends those who denied the resurrection. Those who denied the resurrection did not worship the angels or the messengers; they only worshipped Hubal, al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat. Hubal, al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are all in the Fire.

In any case, whether we say this is a general expression intending a specific meaning, namely those who address the Messenger (ﷺ) and deny the resurrection, or we say it is a general expression that has been specified, there is no doubt that those who are worshipped besides Allah, while they are among the friends of Allah, will not be gathered to the Fire and will not enter it.

﴿and what they used to worship (22) besides Allah, so guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾.

"Guide them" means: direct them. This is guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala), and this does not contradict His saying: ﴿On the Day We gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation (85), and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd﴾ [Maryam 85–86]. For the one who is driven is also guided. Have you seen a man who drives his camel and guides it, or not? He guides it.

These people are driven, and at the same time it is said: "Go this way, go this way, go this way," until they reach the Fire.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has mentioned that these people are driven to the Fire in a state in which they are in need, indeed compelled to seek water.

﴿And We drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd﴾: thirsty. When they arrive, they find nothing but the scorching Fire, and we seek refuge with Allah. This will be like a slap on their faces, for they came hoping to drink, but they are startled by what increases their blaze and thirst. ﴿and what they used to worship (22) besides Allah, so guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾.

﴿Path (sirat)﴾ means a road. The path is of two types: a physical path, which is what feet walk upon, and a spiritual path, which is what hearts walk upon. Whoever remains upright on the spiritual path, following the religion of Allah, will remain upright on the physical path on the Day of Resurrection until he reaches Paradise. Whoever was not upright in the world upon the law of Allah will not be upright in the Hereafter on the road to Paradise, but rather on the road to the Fire here. ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire.﴾ Is the "path" here physical or spiritual?

* Student: Physical.
* Shaykh: Physical. And disbelief?
* Students: Spiritual.
* Shaykh: Spiritual. Good. ﴿to the path of Hellfire﴾. As for His saying ﴿al-Jahim﴾, he said: (the Fire).

So al-Jahim is one of the names of the Fire, and the names of the Fire in the Quran are many and varied. It might be good for us to ask one of you to count them for us from the Quran.

Then He said: ﴿And stop them; indeed they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat 24]. ﴿Stop them﴾ means: detain them, from waqafa yaqifu, and the imperative is qif. (Waqafa) is used intransitively and transitively. When you say: "So-and-so stopped," meaning "so-and-so walked and stopped," is this stopping intransitive or transitive?

* Student: Intransitive.
* Shaykh: Intransitive. And when you say: waqaftu al-qawl (I stopped the statement)?

* Student: Transitive.
* Shaykh: Or waqaftu Zaydan 'inda al-makan al-fulani (I made Zayd stop at such and such place), this is transitive.

﴿Qifuhum﴾ is undoubtedly transitive, and its evidence is that the object pronoun "hum" (them) is in the accusative, and the waw in ﴿qifuhum﴾ is the subject.

We ask the brother: how many letters are in ﴿qifuhum﴾, the number of letters of the verb?

* Student: Two letters.
* Shaykh: Two letters. And how many in the past tense?

* Student: Three.
* Shaykh: And in the present tense?

* Student: Three.
* Shaykh: Three. What do you say?

* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: No, that is not correct. The present tense has two letters, because the letters of present-tense formation (ahruf al-mudara'a) are not counted as part of the root structure of the verb. So the verb (...) has two letters, it stops like this. For this reason it is said: if you want to form the imperative verb, bring its verb in the present, jussive, then delete the present-tense letter.

This benefits the student of knowledge: if you want to form the imperative, take the present-tense verb in the jussive and delete the present-tense prefix. For example, if you want to form the imperative from (khaafa, to fear).

* Student: Khif.
* Shaykh: Khif or khaf?

* Students: Khaf.
* Shaykh: He says: khif. Look at the rule we gave you. Wait, the rule we have given you now: bring the present in the jussive: lam yakhaf, delete the present-tense letter: khaf. (Naam, to sleep.) The imperative: nam or num?

* Students: Nam.
* Student: Num.
* Shaykh: Num. (Hidayat Allah) (...) perhaps you have not broken your fast visibly. Did you break it or not?

* Student: I broke it.
* Shaykh: Good (...). I say: (naam), the imperative: (nam).

Let us apply the rule: lam yanam, delete the yaa of the present: nam.

The imperative of (maala, to incline)?

* Student: Mal.
* Another student: Mil.
* Shaykh: Mil. Good, masha Allah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. The imperative of maala?

* Student: Mil.
* Shaykh: Mil?

* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Good. The proof? Apply the rule.

* Students: Lam yamul.
* Shaykh: Lam yamul.

* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Delete the yaa of the present.

* Students: Mil.
* Shaykh: Mil, correct? Good, we have understood the rule now, and it is a rule that sometimes makes things easy for you. A person may wonder how the imperative of nama becomes nam (...), khaf (...), khif Allah. The answer: because the imperative is derived from the present tense. Its basis is that you bring the present in the jussive and then delete the present-tense letter.

Good. What is the imperative of khasha (to fear)?

* Student: Ikhsh.
* Shaykh: Not ikhsh.
* Student: Ikhsha.
* Shaykh: Ikhsha. Now give me the present in the jussive.

* Students: Lam yakhsha.
* Shaykh: Lam yakhsha. So we must say: ikhsha. Why? Because it is impossible to begin with a sukun (a vowelless letter). If we delete the present-tense yaa, what remains? A silent kha', and the shin is fatha. The silent kha' can never be pronounced at the beginning (...). When you find a word whose first letter is silent, you must bring the hamzat al-wasl (connecting hamza). Then you say?

* Student: Ikhsha.
* Shaykh: Ikhsha, yes. Good.

And the imperative of (rama, to throw)?

* Students: Irmi.
* Shaykh: Irmi, because the present is lam yarmi, which begins with a sukun, so the hamza must be brought. And Allah knows best.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Shaykh, regarding (...).
* Shaykh: No, this is the language of the Arabs, that the hamzat al-wasl, when a word begins with it, is kasra.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, give (a'ta yu'ti, from a'ta, to give). This hamza is not hamzat al-wasl; it is hamzat al-qat' (a cutting hamza).
* Student: (...), O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Those who ascend the Sirat are all believers, but it is the sinful believers who fall into the Fire. As for the people of the Fire, who are its people, they (...) before the Sirat.
* Student: They do not pass over it?
* Shaykh: They do not pass over the Sirat. No, only one who crossed the Sirat in the world crosses it. But whoever crossed it in a sound manner, crossed. And whoever kept stumbling into sins, he is the one who (...).

* * *

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled." (18) It will be but one shout, and at once they will be looking﴾ [al-Saffat 18–19].

﴿Na'am (yes)﴾: what is its grammatical analysis (i'rab)?

* Student: Its i'rab?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...) object (...) subject.
* Shaykh: It is not a subject.
* Student: A particle of response.
* Shaykh: A particle of response (...). Where did we stop?

* Students: At ﴿qifuhum﴾.
* Shaykh: At ﴿qifuhum﴾. Good. ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾. What is meant by ﴿path of Hellfire﴾?

* Student: The road to Hellfire.
* Shaykh: The road to Hellfire, meaning the road that leads to Hellfire, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. Let us take the benefits of the verses, I think:

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ [al-Saffat 18].

In this noble verse there is evidence of the importance of answering those who question, when they die and become dust and bones: will they be resurrected or not? The reason is that Allah commanded His Prophet with a specific command concerning their answer. We have mentioned earlier that when Allah commands His Prophet with a specific command, it indicates the importance of that command, because the basic principle is that the entire Quran was commanded to be conveyed by the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. So when a verse comes in which Allah says "Say," this is a specific command to convey it, and it indicates concern with this matter and that it is of great importance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory to refute the doubts of the people of falsehood, because Allah did not say "leave them," but said: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who deny the resurrection will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in humiliation, as His saying shows: ﴿and you will be humbled﴾. We have mentioned during the exegesis several verses indicating that they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in abasement, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and you will see them presented before it, humbled by humiliation, looking with a sidelong glance﴾ [al-Shura 45].

* Among the benefits of the verse: those who believe in this will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection honored, and the reasoning is that if the recompense of these deniers is to be gathered in disgrace and humiliation, then the opposite will be the opposite. Recompense is of the same kind as the deed, so the believers will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection honored.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It will be but one shout﴾ [al-Saffat 19], to the end of the verses.

* What is derived from these verses, first: a demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for all of creation will come out with one shout. This is one, and all of creation will come out immediately without delay. In this is evidence of power from two aspects:

The first aspect: the command is not repeated.

The second aspect: the swiftness of obedience and compliance with the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: people will come out on the Day of Resurrection and look, either with the look of the eye or with waiting. Whichever it is, it indicates that they come out to a strange matter, because they were first in their graves.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, it indicates that they come out to a matter they were not accustomed to, because they were first in their graves, then they were gathered to something strange that they did not know before; as He said: ﴿and at once they will be looking﴾ [al-Saffat 19].

* Among the benefits of the verses: these deniers will call out on the Day of Resurrection with woe, destruction, and ruin, as shown by their saying: ﴿O woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Saffat 20], as Allah said in another verse: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions﴾ [al-Furqan 14].

* Among the benefits of the verses: the confirmation of this statement, and that it is a matter that will certainly occur as if it were present, as shown by His saying: ﴿And they will say, "O woe to us!"﴾ [al-Saffat 20]. He expressed the future with the past tense to confirm that it will certainly happen.

* Among the benefits of the verses: that people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and recompensed for their deeds. This is derived from His saying: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾. This will be the outcome for all creation: that they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and recompensed for their deeds, and that this recompense will be final, with no action after it and no term beyond it; as He said: ﴿This is the Day of Recompense﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verses: the Day of Resurrection is a Day of Judgment, meaning a day of ruling between people and distinguishing some from others; as He said: ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾ [al-Saffat 21].

* Also among the benefits of the verses: the rebuke of these deniers; as He said: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [al-Saffat 21]. The reasoning behind the rebuke is that when a person witnesses what he denied, he will say to whoever led him to this denial, or agreed with him: "Look at it yourself! You said it was a lie and would not happen; look at it now, it has happened!" This will increase his regret and remorse for not believing in this day.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: on the Day of Resurrection people will be distinguished from one another, and some kinds, forms and peers will be gathered together; as He said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat 22]. This is part of the distinction that Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: these deniers will not benefit from their gathering together and the gathering of some of them to others, such-and-such (...); as He said in another verse: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you will be sharing in the punishment﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39].

In the world, if someone shares a punishment with you, it benefits you, either because he bears a part of that punishment for you, or because you find comfort in it; for the befalling of calamity upon others consoles you and helps you bear that calamity and be patient with it, as al-Khansa said about her brother Sakhr:

"They do not weep the like of my brother, but I console my soul for him with consolation."

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the humiliation of these polytheists by gathering their idols into the Fire. The reasoning is that humiliating the object of worship is a humiliation for the worshipper. Let me give you an example: if there is a master who has slaves beneath him, or a man who has a family beneath him, and this man is humiliated, the one with the family or the one with the slaves is humiliated. Is that a humiliation?

* Student: For the family.
* Shaykh: For the family and for the slaves, because they say: "This is our elder and our great one whom we honor." So if he is humiliated, it is a humiliation for us, even if it is not a physical humiliation but a psychological and moral one. In the same way these idols are humiliated, which is a humiliation for their worshippers.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is permissible to mention a general term even if it includes what is not intended, when it is clarified in another place.

This leads to the principle that clarification (bayan) does not have to coincide with the thing being clarified. What is impermissible in clarification is delaying it beyond the time of need. If it is clarified at the time of need, that prohibited matter is removed. This has been made clear in many verses of the Qur'an, that believers will not enter the Fire: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] from Us has preceded, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya 101]. Every verse that promises believers and the God-fearing prevents these people from entering the Fire, even if they used to worship others besides Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these disbelieving polytheists will be gathered toward the path of Hell. Just as in this world they chose the path of the people of the Fire, in the Hereafter they will be repaid in kind, so they will be guided down to the path of the Blazing Fire and turned away from the path of the people of Bliss.

* * *

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And stop them, for indeed they are to be questioned﴾ [as-Saffat 24]. He said: (Hold them back at the path). The command is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the address appears to be to the angels, since the angels are the ones who manage creation by the command of Allah. So it is said to the angels: Stop these disbelieving polytheists who associated partners with Allah. ﴿And stop them﴾ means: cause them to stand, i.e., hold them back. ﴿For indeed they are to be questioned﴾ (about all their statements and actions). The phrase ﴿for indeed they are to be questioned﴾ may either be general, as the author said, meaning that they are questioned about their statements, their deeds, their polytheism, their deviation, and all their conditions; or it may be specified by His saying: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾ [as-Saffat 25], in which case the matter they are questioned about is one thing, namely that they are stopped and questioned in this manner as a rebuke and reproach, as the author said: (It will be said to them in rebuke: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾, i.e., one of you does not help another). So the verse, in reality, admits of two meanings.

The first meaning: you are questioned about what?
* Students: About conditions.
* Shaykh: About all conditions and deeds. Or you are questioned with this question, namely ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾. Whichever it is, the verse contains reproach and mockery of them, since it is said to them: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾ Today? In the world you used to help one another. Those who worship these idols defend them, as passed over us at the end of Surat Ya-Sin: ﴿They are unable to help them, while they are a gathered army for them﴾ [Ya-Sin 75]. The worshippers defend the gods, just as Abu Sufyan said before he embraced Islam, at the Battle of Uhud: "Uluw Hubal" [Exalt Hubal], [Narrated by al-Bukhari (4043) from the hadith of al-Bara'.] He boasted of it and defended it. So it will be said on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾, meaning: what is it that prevents you from helping one another? The answer is clear, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Rather, they are today submitting﴾ [as-Saffat 26], meaning: humbled and submissive. This sentence introduced by ﴿Rather﴾ indicates a shift from one style to another. That is, they do not help one another because today they are submitting, they and their idols, humbled and abased.

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾ (one of you does not help another as you did in the world). ﴿Rather, they are today submitting﴾. The interrogative in ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾ is intended for reproach and mockery, meaning: where is the help you gave one another in the world? Will you not help one another today? The answer: they cannot help one another, because they are humiliated and submitting. ﴿Rather, they are today submitting﴾, i.e., (submitting) to the judgment of Allah concerning them as a recompense, and to the judgment of Allah concerning them by decree.

﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾ [as-Saffat 27]. Meaning: ﴿they will approach one another﴾, i.e., some of them will turn toward others. The clause ﴿questioning each other﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to the subject and the object: the subject is in ﴿some of them﴾ and the object is in (toward some). They will turn to one another, questioning one another with blame and enmity. Having been in agreement and friendship in the world, they will become enemies in the Hereafter: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf 67].

﴿Questioning each other﴾: one asks another in a manner of reproach and denial. He says: (they dispute with one another).

(﴿They will say﴾, i.e., the followers among them to the leaders: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾ [as-Saffat 28], from the direction from which we used to feel secure because of your oaths that you were upon the truth, so we believed you and followed you. The meaning: you misled us.) Some of them began questioning others. The followers question the followers, and the leaders question the followers, and all of them question one another, because they have fallen into bewilderment. Some say to others, namely the followers, saying: ﴿Indeed, you used to come﴾: ﴿Indeed, you﴾ is addressed to the leaders by those who followed them. ﴿Used to﴾ means in the world. ﴿Come to us﴾ means in your speech to us and your calling us. ﴿From the right﴾: ("from" here denotes "passing from," i.e., you came to us in an approach issuing from the right. So what is meant by "the right"?)

It has been said: the right here means oaths, based on His saying: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾ [al-Baqarah 224], the plural of "yamin" [oath]. So the meaning of ﴿from the right﴾ is from oaths; that is, the leaders swear to the followers that they are upon the truth. This is like the saying of Allah about Satan: ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors"﴾ [al-A'raf 21].

It has also been said: the right here means goodness, from "yumn" [blessing], which is optimism. That is, you promise us good and say: "Follow us, for if you follow us you will attain honor and victory." So you promise us good, while you are lying against us.

It has also been said: the right here means strength, as in His saying: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right﴾ [as-Saffat 93], i.e., with force. And it has been said: with the right hand. So ﴿al-yamin﴾ has three opinions:
The first opinion?
* Students: Oaths.
* Shaykh: Oaths. The second?
* Students: Goodness.
* Shaykh: Goodness. The third?
* Students: Strength.
* Shaykh: Strength. The truth is that all these meanings apply from the leaders: they swear to the followers that they are upon the truth; they address them through force, since they are leaders; and they also promise them good, saying: follow us and you will have honor and victory, and the like. So the verse includes all three meanings. The followers say to the leaders: you come to us from this direction, the right: oaths, or force, or goodness. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, says in explaining it: from the direction by which we used to feel secure from you. His statement is suitable for all three meanings, because people feel secure when they swear oaths, feel secure when they promise good, and feel secure when they are powerful, because the weak generally believe that the strong is right, and that he reached this position or rank because he is in the right.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿They will say﴾, i.e.) what?
* Student: (The followed).
* Shaykh: I mean, the ones being followed? In your language, is it the leaders?
* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: In any case, "the leaders" (al-matbu'un) is clearer than "the followed" (al-muttaba'un), because "al-muttaba'un" might be confused with the one who follows, i.e., the followers. In reality, the one who said it is the leaders. (﴿They will say﴾, i.e., the followed say to them: ﴿No, you were not believers﴾ [as-Saffat 29], and our misguiding you would only be true if you had been believers and then turned back from faith to us.) That is, the leaders said to these followers: ﴿No﴾ here is for negation, to nullify what they claimed in their statement: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾. The meaning: No, we did not come to you from the right, but ﴿you were not believers﴾. Had you been believers, your statement would be true: we misled you. But since you were not believers from the start, the fault is from us against you, or from you against yourselves?
* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: (...) The leaders said: ﴿No, you were not believers﴾, because the followers had claimed that these leaders were the ones who misled them: they misled them by force, or by promise of good, or by oaths, or the like.

So the followed said to the followers: ﴿No﴾, meaning there is no truth to what you said, because ("no" is for nullification) ﴿you were not believers﴾ at all, so that we could mislead you. Misguidance can only be true if it befalls a believer and someone misleads him. But if he was not a believer at all, then the fault is from himself, not from another. For this reason the author, may Allah have mercy on him, says: (﴿No, you were not believers﴾, and our misguiding you would only be true) when?
(if you had been believers and then turned back from faith to us). The leaders now disassociate themselves from what? From the followers, and place the blame on whom? On the followers themselves. They say, as Satan says: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I betrayed you. And I had no authority over you, except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves"﴾ [Ibrahim 22]. We seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan.

These leaders say what Satan said. They say to the followers: You are the ones who misled yourselves. As for us, we did not mislead you, because we did not address a people who were believers and then mislead them after their faith. Rather, we addressed a people who submitted to disbelief by their own choice, so the blame is on them for themselves, not on us. This explains His saying: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their bonds are cut off﴾ [al-Baqarah 166].

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So guide them to the path of the Blazing Fire (23). And stop them, for indeed they are to be questioned﴾ [as-Saffat 23–24].

In this verse and what follows there are benefits:
* First: when the angels drive these disbelievers to the Fire, they humiliate them in several ways. They make them stand on the path, i.e., at it. You know that making someone stand, and saying "stop," "go," "walk," and the like, involves humiliation, since the person is in another's hand like a tool.
* Another benefit: they are humiliated in another, moral way. It is said to them: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another?﴾, i.e., what prevents you today from helping one another after you used to help one another in the world? In this there is humiliation, reproach, and blame that is clear.
* Another benefit: these people in that situation are humbled and submissive, as He said: ﴿Rather, they are today submitting﴾ [as-Saffat 26]. In the world they were arrogant, not accepting the truth, but disputing and offering their necks for killing against the truth, may Allah protect us. But in the Hereafter they are submitting.
* Among the benefits of these verses: these disbelievers blame one another and curse one another. Allah the Exalted even said in another verse: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-Ankabut 25]; this is because of His saying: ﴿They will say: Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾ [as-Saffat 28].
* Among its benefits: the explanation of the methods that misleaders use, which are varied: sometimes by force, sometimes by deception, gentleness, and promising good, and sometimes by emphasis that what they are upon is the truth. If you look at the reality of the Christians today and other people of misguidance who misguide others, you will know how this verse applies to these callers to evil. The Christians, for example, who call themselves "missionaries," and they are truthful, yet we say: they are bearers of good news of a painful punishment. They promise people good, open schools, and lavish money on people in order to mislead them and take them out [of Islam], and they exploit the opportunity of poverty and ignorance in such matters.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these leaders repeat the reproach upon the followers, as they say to them: ﴿No, you were not believers﴾ [as-Saffat 29]. So the calamity is from yourselves, not from us.

And among the benefits of the verse is that whoever's faith is not firmly established, false propaganda affects him, because a believer whose faith is firm is not misled by propaganda, and cannot be turned away from the faith he held. This is according to His saying: ﴿Rather, you were not [truly] believers﴾. Had you been truly believers with a steadfast faith, our misguidance would not have affected you. The believer would accept death even if he were thrown from a high place, and he would not disbelieve in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. But one whose faith is shaky, unstable and not firmly rooted, this is the one whom these propaganda campaigns mislead. ﴿Rather, you were not believers (29). And We had no authority over you﴾ [As-Saffat 29–30]. Is this the beginning of the lesson?
