**Shaykh:** It is not possible. Therefore, there must be a trial and a test by which the extent of a person's patience is known, so that he is rewarded according to the amount of patience that came from him.

Another benefit of this noble verse: the virtue of Abraham and Ishmael, which has been mentioned before. But from this verse their virtue becomes clear, in that they were patient with this trial, patient with the patience of the noble, and submitted, and nothing remained but to carry it out, until relief came from Allah, glorified and exalted.

Another benefit of the noble verses in His saying: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾ [As-Saffat 107]: the demonstration that the lifting of the killing or the sacrifice from the son was made in exchange for completing the execution and obedience. This was that Abraham was commanded to slaughter a ransom for his son, and this slaughtered animal would be great. For this reason He said: ﴿We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, meaning: We commanded him to slaughter a great sacrifice as a ransom for him.

Another benefit of this verse, according to what some scholars deduced: if a person vows to slaughter his son, it is obligatory upon him to slaughter a ram as a ransom for him. He said: because this is what Allah commanded Abraham, that it be a ransom for his son. It is known that if a person vows to slaughter his son, it is not lawful for him to fulfill it, because it is a vow of disobedience, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him." [Reported by al-Bukhari (6696) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] So what should he do? They said: he slaughters a ram, as Abraham was commanded. This deduction is good, were it not that it contradicts the apparent sunnah, which is that whoever vows an act of disobedience is forbidden from doing it, but must make the expiation for an oath. So if someone says: "I vow to Allah that I will slaughter the first son who comes to me," and then a son comes to him, it is not lawful for him to slaughter him, but we say: you must—according to the preponderant view—make the expiation for an oath.

Another benefit of the verses in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We left for him among later generations﴾ [As-Saffat 108] and ﴿Peace be upon Abraham﴾ [As-Saffat 109]: Allah the Exalted preserved for Abraham, peace be upon him, a good commendation and peace among later generations. A good commendation, by which he is praised for what came from him of calling to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and patience with the trial that befell him without his choice, and patience with the trial that befell him by his choice. Among the trial that befell him without his choice was burning, when his people said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods﴾ [Al-Anbiya 68]. You know what happens to a person when he is resolved to be burned or set on fire for the sake of calling to Allah, because he will suffer for it both physical pain and heartfelt pain.

Indeed, among us is one who, when he sees people not accepting his call, is pained merely because they did not accept it. How much more so when they reject it and burn him for its sake, or burn him because of it! Is this not a greater pain upon the heart?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Good. So this is undoubtedly a trial. Yet he was patient, and he was cast into the fire, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded that it become coolness and peace upon him.

The second trial, which came by his choice, was the command to slaughter his son and his resolve to carry it out.

Good. This is from the good commendation of Abraham.

Likewise, Abraham is a figure upon whom the nations agree to praise, and whom none should blame. For this reason He said: ﴿Peace be upon Abraham﴾ [As-Saffat 109].

If you say: We, this nation, greet Abraham and others, saying "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When you say that, you have greeted every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (831) and Muslim (402/55) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]

The answer: we greet every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth. But our greeting upon Abraham and the like of the resolute messengers (Ulul-Azm, the messengers of great steadfastness) is more emphatic and more eloquent than our greeting upon the general body of the righteous.

Among the lessons of the verse, in His words: ﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [as-Saffat 110], is that Allah, exalted is He, repeated this sentence, which conveys this ruling, to encourage people to do good. From this it is derived that whoever speaks about a matter that is to be encouraged should repeat it, because when a ruling is repeated, souls grow more settled in it and more eager for it. In the context of warning, likewise, it is repeated. Have you not seen His words in Surat al-Mursalat: ﴿Woe that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat 15]? It is repeated several times as a warning and admonition. So for every situation there is a fitting speech. Repetition may be feeble and far from eloquence, but when it occurs in a place where it is becoming, it is part of eloquence. Here Allah repeated this sentence, ﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [as-Saffat 110], in several verses.

Among the lessons of the verses: in His words: ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ [as-Saffat 111], is the praise of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, with these two attributes: servitude ('ubudiyyah) and faith (iman).

From this it follows that whoever possesses servitude and faith receives praise in proportion to what he possesses of them. The more a person is devoted to Allah in worship and the more he believes in Him, the greater and more abundant the praise upon him. Do not be deceived by the opposition you encounter in this world, for this may come, but what is it? A trial and a test. And praise may come even after a person's death. How many imams of this Ummah were harmed during their lives, yet after their deaths the recompense for that harm was that Allah raised their remembrance. The evidence for this is abundant, and many of you know a great deal of it: that many imams of this Ummah were harmed for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, suffered blows, and were hurt by word and deed, yet the final outcome was theirs and good praise came after their deaths.

Among the lessons of this noble verse: the virtue of servitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and of faith in Him. Without doubt, the purpose of His words: ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ [as-Saffat 111] is praise of him. When praise, or rather a ruling, is attached to an attribute, it grows strong with that attribute's strength and weakens with its weakness. So when praise is attached to servitude and faith, the more a person is intensely and strongly devoted in worship, the more deserving he is of praise; and the more a person is strong in faith, the more deserving he is of praise, and vice versa.

Among the lessons of the noble verses: in His words: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾ [as-Saffat 112], is the legitimacy of giving glad tidings of a child, which has already been mentioned, because a person is without doubt gladdened by a child, especially when he is given the good news that the child will be a prophet, as in this verse: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous﴾, or that he is ﴿a forbearing boy﴾ [as-Saffat 101], as in the verses concerning Ismail.

Among the lessons of the noble verse: the clear evidence that the one Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice was Ismail and not Isaac. We explained in the previous lesson nine aspects which indicate that the one commanded to be sacrificed was Ismail.

Among the lessons of the noble verse: the affirmation of the prophethood of Isaac, from His words: ﴿Isaac, a prophet﴾ [as-Saffat 112].

Among its lessons: a person may be given prophethood while still a child at the time of his birth. How? ﴿a prophet﴾ — we say: this state is future-determined (muqaddarah), not a contemporaneous state (hal haliyyah) but a future state, as passed over us in yesterday's tafsir. Thus, the lesson derived from it is that when giving glad tidings, a person should mention what is hoped for in the future from that which he has been given good news of, whether it is a child, wealth, a wife, a house, or other than that.
The main point is that when a person expects good in the future regarding what he has been given good news of, he should link that to the glad tidings, because Allah linked His prophethood with the glad tidings of him.

Among the lessons of this verse: the praise of Isaac, peace be upon him, for being a prophet from among the righteous. The prophets, peace be upon them, combined righteousness in themselves with reforming their nations; they are righteous and reformers.

Among the lessons of the noble verse: prophethood is an attribute of perfection, because Allah, exalted is He, linked it with glad tidings. Were it not an attribute of perfection through which a person is gladdened, mentioning it would be vain, with no benefit in it.

Among the lessons of the noble verses, in His words: ﴿And We blessed him and Isaac﴾ [as-Saffat 113]: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, blessed Ibrahim and Isaac. Among the blessings upon Ibrahim is that all the prophets after him were from his offspring, by His words: ﴿And We sent Noah and Ibrahim, and We placed in their offspring prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-Hadid 26]. As for those before Ibrahim, they are from the offspring of Noah; as for those after him, they are from the offspring of Noah and Ibrahim. Is that so, or do you not agree with me?
* A student: After him, O Shaykh, the offspring of Isaac.
* The Shaykh: How? Here, in "from their offspring," who are they?
* Students: Isaac and Ibrahim.
* The Shaykh: Good. Whoever is not from the offspring of Isaac is from the offspring of Ibrahim. My mind went to Noah. Whoever is not from the offspring of Isaac is from the offspring of Ibrahim, and whoever is from the offspring of Isaac is from the offspring of Ibrahim and Isaac.
An example of one who was not from the offspring of Isaac: Ismail and Muhammad ﷺ, for they are from the offspring of Ibrahim and not from the offspring of Isaac. As for the prophets of the Children of Israel, they are all from the offspring of Isaac.

Among the lessons of His words: ﴿And among their offspring is one who does good and one who clearly wrongs himself﴾ [as-Saffat 113]: among them is that the offspring of Ibrahim and Isaac divide into two categories: the doer of good and the wrongdoer. This includes absolute good and general good, and absolute wrong and general wrong. Is that so? Good. Or we may say: absolute good is shared with absolute wrong, or absolute wrong is shared with it, because whoever combines good deeds and bad deeds has in him general good and general wrong. That is, he does not have complete good, because he has wrong, and he does not have absolute wrong, because he has good. So absolute good and absolute wrong are opposites.
Absolute good is one who, if he commits a sin, remembers Allah and seeks forgiveness, and the effect of the sin is lifted from him.
Absolute wrong is the disbeliever who wrongs himself through disbelief, as Allah says: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah 254].
So the offspring of Ibrahim and Isaac, when detailed, divide into three categories: the absolutely good, and the absolutely wrongdoing. The absolutely good is the Muslim, or rather the believer: ﴿Those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Ali 'Imran 135].
The second is the absolute wrongdoer, who is the disbeliever. There remains one who has general good, who is the believer or Muslim who has sins, and general wrong, who is likewise the believer or Muslim who has sins. If his sins outweigh his acts of obedience, he is closer to wrong; if his acts of obedience outweigh his sins, he is closer to good.

Among the lessons of the noble verse: ﴿and one who clearly wrongs himself﴾ [as-Saffat 113]: wrong may be manifest or may show its doer, depending on the meaning of ﴿clearly﴾ — whether it means evident, or means revealing the wrongdoing of its doer. Wrong may be an obvious, plain wrong, such as aggression against people's wealth, blood, and honor, and in that case the man reveals his wrong. It may also be hidden, which a person conceals, and this is a clear wrong with respect to him, but it does not reveal him, since he has hidden it from people. And Allah knows best.

[[The author's words have been abridged due to their great length]]

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.﴾ [al-Saffat 133].

In this verse and those that follow in the narrative, [we learn] that Lot, peace be upon him, was one of the messengers. It has already passed in our commentary that he was sent to a people who committed the abomination (al-fahisha), which is the mounting of males among the worlds, and who abandoned what Allah had created for them of spouses.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the concern of the Lord, mighty and majestic, with eliminating base morals, for their abomination necessitated that Allah send to them a messenger to refute it and eradicate it.

* Among the benefits of these verses: in His saying ﴿when We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ [al-Saffat 134], [we learn] that Allah, glorified and exalted, saves those who fear Him by their achievement [of salvation], and that Allah saved Lot and his family except his wife. It follows from this that a believing person should give precedence to hope when he has fulfilled the right of Allah; this is seen in that Allah, glorified and exalted, saved His sincere believing servants from the punishment of the deniers who were arrogant.

* Among the benefits of these verses: a disbelieving woman may be under a believing man without him knowing; this is shown by His saying ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Saffat 135]. Allah has explained the cause of this—that is, the cause of the punishment befalling her—by stating that she had betrayed her husband through disbelief without his knowledge.

It follows from this benefit that a person should keep watch over his family, investigate, and probe their affairs so that he does not fall into betrayal, whether it is betrayal of honour or betrayal of religion.

* Among the benefits of these verses: in His saying ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ [al-Saffat 136], [there is] a warning against a person doing the deeds of these people and thereby being destroyed. The destruction of Lot's people was physical, but those who resemble them may be destroyed in a moral sense, and may also be destroyed physically; Allah may, for example, send upon them thunderbolts, hail, and other things that destroy them. But moral destruction is certain. And how is moral destruction in this abomination? By males being transformed into females, for these who are sodomized—may Allah protect us—become exactly like women: he himself seeks men and pursues them, hoping they will do it to him, may Allah protect us, because he has become transformed and is exactly like a woman. There is no doubt that this is a destruction of manhood and a corruption of society.

* Among the benefits of these verses: in His saying ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾ [al-Saffat 137], [there is] an indication that when a person sees a thing with his own eyes, his certainty is stronger than when he is merely told about it. [This is shown] by His saying ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾, and you witness their traces. This is called the certainty of sight (haqq al-yaqin), and being told of it is called the certainty of knowledge (ilm al-yaqin).

He said: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [al-Saffat 137–138]. It may be said that this contains evidence or an indication that travelling in the morning is better than travelling at the end of the day, by His saying ﴿in the morning (137) and at night﴾. This is if we say that by "morning" is meant the specific time, namely the early part of the day. But if we say that by "morning" is meant the whole day, and that the part is used to denote the whole, as the author indicated, then there is no evidence in that.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the permissibility of travelling by night. The reasoning is that Allah affirmed them, saying ﴿and at night﴾. However, this benefit is open to question, because Allah, exalted is He, is speaking about the deeds of these deniers; it may be said that the purpose is to establish the proof against them, not to approve of them. Nevertheless, the Sunnah has indicated the permissibility of walking at night.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebuke of one who does not take heed, [for his] foolishness and lack of intellect; by His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 138].

* Among its benefits: intellect (aql) in reality is that which guides its possessor to doing good and abandoning evil. Intellect is not cleverness (dhaka'), for intellect is one thing and cleverness is another. Anyone who denies the messengers and is arrogant toward what they brought is not intelligent, even if he is among the most cunning of people. Is that not so? Yes: a person who denies the messengers and is arrogant toward what they brought is not intelligent, even if he is clever, and even if he is of noble standing and rank, he is not intelligent; by His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾. Allah said something similar about the Children of Israel, who commanded people to righteousness while forgetting themselves, though they recite the Book: ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah 44]. And Allah is the Granter of success.

* A student: (...) ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Saffat 135]. Is this a disparagement of her (...)?

* The Shaykh: You mean, did He say that as a form of disparagement and blame, or to explain her reality? As for our present usage, it is considered disparagement; but apparently in the Arabic language it is not considered disparagement, for they say "shaykh" and they say "ajuz" (old woman), and they do not regard that as disparagement. But among us it is considered disparagement by custom.

* A student: (...) ﴿among those who remained behind﴾?

* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿among those who remained behind﴾, among those left behind in the punishment, because he had been commanded to leave the town except his wife.

This is called the certainty of sight (haqq al-yaqin), and being told of it is called the certainty of knowledge (ilm al-yaqin).

He said: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [al-Saffat 137–138]. It may be said that this contains evidence or an indication that travelling in the morning is better than travelling at the end of the day, by His saying ﴿in the morning (137) and at night﴾. This is if we say that by "morning" is meant the specific time, namely the early part of the day. But if we say that by "morning" is meant the whole day, and that the part is used to denote the whole, as the author indicated, then there is no evidence in that.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the permissibility of travelling by night. The reasoning is that Allah affirmed them, saying ﴿and at night﴾. However, this benefit is open to question, because Allah, exalted is He, is speaking about the deeds of these deniers; it may be said that the purpose is to establish the proof against them, not to approve of them. Nevertheless, the Sunnah has indicated the permissibility of walking at night.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebuke of one who does not take heed, [for his] foolishness and lack of intellect; by His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 138].

* Among its benefits: intellect (aql) in reality is that which guides its possessor to doing good and abandoning evil. Intellect is not cleverness (dhaka'), for intellect is one thing and cleverness is another. Anyone who denies the messengers and is arrogant toward what they brought is not intelligent, even if he is among the most cunning of people. Is that not so? Yes: a person who denies the messengers and is arrogant toward what they brought is not intelligent, even if he is clever, and even if he is of noble standing and rank, he is not intelligent; by His saying ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾. Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers. When he fled to the laden ship, and he drew lots and was among the losers, so the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected. So We threw him onto the open shore while he was sick, and We caused to grow over him a gourd vine, and We sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time. So ask them: Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?﴾ [As-Saffat 139–149].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers﴾. This sentence is emphasized with two emphatics: the first is (inna) and the second is the lam. The reason for the emphasis is that the establishment of prophethood is something that many people deny, and what is denied must be emphasized with what proves its establishment, whether by verbal emphasis through emphatic particles, or by semantic emphasis through mention of the signs and evidences that prove it. The prophets, peace be upon them, have had their prophethood established by both kinds; that is, by verbal emphasis and by semantic emphasis. So Allah the Exalted supported them with cosmic and legal signs, and Allah supported their message with verbal emphatics, as in this verse. He said: ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers﴾, meaning among the people whom Allah the Exalted sent to His servants. He did not specify to whom he was sent, but it is mentioned in other verses that he was sent to his people. Likewise it is authentically related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that "every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, but I have been sent to all people"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. Jonah is one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, whom Allah the Exalted sent to his people, and its explanation of his story will come, Allah willing, here. Then He said: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾.

﴿When he fled﴾. The author said: (fled ﴿to the laden ship﴾, the filled ship, when he became angry at his people), to the end. His saying ﴿when he fled﴾ may mean that (idh) is connected to "the messengers", i.e., among the messengers in this state, meaning that his fleeing did not strip him of the message. It may also be connected to an implied verb, with the sense: "Remember when he fled to the laden ship." This is better: that it is connected to an implied verb, because when He established his messengership, He mentioned one of his states, namely his fleeing, peace be upon him. Based on this, we say: ﴿when he fled﴾ is not connected to "the messengers", because his messengership was before he fled, but it is connected to an implied verb, the meaning being: remember when he fled. Al-Ibaq is fleeing, and it seems he, peace be upon him, went out hastily because he went out angry with his people when they did not believe and the punishment did not descend upon them.

He said: ﴿the laden ship﴾. The ship (al-fulk) means the vessel, which are the watercraft. Allah has blessed the servants with the ship that runs on the sea by His command, carrying provisions from one place to another, and Allah has bestowed it upon the servants as a favor, and His grace is great in our present age. The ship in our present age is not like the ship of the past. The ship of the past depended on sails and wind, had obstacles, and had great dangers. As for the ship now, it is the opposite of that. Allah has also favored His servants with ships in our present age, in that these vessels have diversified: they have become a water vessel, a land vessel, and an air vessel. The air vessel is the aircraft, the land is vehicles, and the water is ships, and all of this falls under His saying the Exalted: ﴿And He has made for you of ships and livestock that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them, and say: Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 12–13].

And His saying: ﴿the laden ship﴾. The author said: (the filled ship), meaning ﴿the laden﴾ in the sense of filled with passengers. So he boarded the sea (angry with his people, when the punishment he had promised them did not descend upon them, so he boarded the ship, and it stopped in the depths of the sea. The sailors said: here is a slave who has fled from his master; the lot will reveal him). Thus said the author, may Allah have mercy on him: that the ship stopped in the depths of the sea, and its stopping was because of Jonah's fleeing. The sailors said, and they were the ship's captains: here is a slave who has fled from his master; the lot will reveal him. However, what the author mentioned has no evidence for it, and it is one of the distant Israelite narrations. Rather, when this laden ship was in the open sea, and it was laden and filled, and it reached the depths of the sea, the load became heavy. When the load becomes heavy, one of two things must happen: either the load is lightened, or everyone drowns. There is no doubt that lightening the load is preferable to everyone drowning, because if the load is lightened, those who remain are saved, and if the load remains as it is, everyone drowns. The survival of some is preferable to the destruction of all. This is a matter of reason. They drew lots, meaning it was not preferable to cast some of them into the sea rather than others, so there was no way to escape this problem except by lot. So they drew lots.

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾ [As-Saffat 141]. They drew lots as to who would be cast out. It is known that when we know who will be cast out, we know who will remain. For this reason Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Sahama means (he cast lots with the people of the ship). ﴿And was among the losers﴾ (those overcome by the lot, so they cast him into the sea). The apparent sense of the author's presentation, may Allah have mercy on him, is that no one was cast out except Jonah. But the verse indicates otherwise than what the author's words indicate, because His saying ﴿and was among the losers﴾, here the (min) is partitive, meaning: one of them. This indicates that the lot fell upon him and also fell upon others. So the matter is now clear: the ship was laden, and the ship must sink unless some of its passengers are cast out. Casting out some passengers is preferable to the destruction of all. There is no way to cast out some by specific designation, because if we designated one person over another, that would be injustice, and the one designated would refuse, and it would become a dispute, and perhaps the ship would sink in the midst of this dispute. So what is the way to designate who is cast out? It is the lot.

So they drew lots, and the lot fell upon some people, and some people were saved from it, and Jonah was among those whom the lot fell upon: ﴿and was among the losers﴾, so he was cast into the sea.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿Then the fish swallowed him﴾, it swallowed him, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, meaning: he did what he was to be blamed for, by going to the sea and boarding the ship without permission from his Lord). The fish swallowed him in one piece, and did not chew him, because if it had chewed him he would have been broken and perished. But Allah subjected this fish to him, so it swallowed him whole and gulped him down, until he reached the place of its belly without any harm befalling him. As for His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, the clause here is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in His saying (swallowed him), not from the subject of (swallowed). Because the subject is who? The fish, and the fish is not blameworthy. The blameworthy one is the one swallowed.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾, meaning Jonah. The meaning of ﴿blameworthy﴾ is one who does what he is to be blamed for, just as one says "munajjid" for someone who has entered Najd, for example. So mufʿil may come to mean being characterized by something. The blameworthy one is the one who did what he deserved blame for. And what is he blamed for? That he left his people angry with them before Allah had given him permission, and it was obligatory for him to be patient. For this reason Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was suppressing grief. Had not a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast out onto the open shore while he was blameworthy. But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾ [Al-Qalam 48–50]. The point is that Jonah, peace be upon him, was swallowed by the fish in a state for which he was blameworthy. What is the basis of that? What is the basis of that?

* Student: That he went out angry from his people without permission from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [As-Saffat 142–144]. (Lawla) occurs often in the Qur'an, in the Sunnah, and in people's speech, so what is it? I say: (lawla) comes in several senses. First: it is a particle of prohibition due to existence, meaning its consequent is prevented because its condition exists: (Lawla Allah ma ihtadayna), the non-guidance is negated because of Allah's existence. This is common. It is said: a particle of prohibition due to existence. Its two counterparts are (law) and (lamma): (lamma) is a particle of existence due to existence, and (law) is a particle of prohibition due to prohibition. So (law), (lamma) and (lawla) each indicate something shared with the others. For example, (law) is a particle of prohibition due to prohibition: you say, "Law jaʾa Zaydun la-akramtuh", what is prohibited? The honoring, due to the non-existence of the coming. And you say: "Lamma jaʾa Zaydun akramtuh": this is a particle of existence due to existence; the honoring existed due to the existence of the coming, is that right? And you say: "Lawla majiʾ Zaydin la-akramtu Fulanan": a particle of prohibition due to existence. What is prohibited? The honoring of Fulan, due to the existence of Zayd's coming.

Here: ﴿Then had it not been that he was of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained﴾. What is prohibited? The remaining, due to the existence of glorification. Had it not been that he, that is Jonah, ﴿was of those who glorify Allah﴾ (those who remember Him much in the belly of the fish, saying: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers"). That is, had it not been that he was among those who glorified Allah with this wording or with other wording, and it is better to say: with this wording or with other wording, meaning he was among those who glorify Allah, either before the fish swallowed him, or during his presence in the belly of the fish. Had it not been for this, ﴿he would have remained in its belly﴾, i.e., in the belly of the fish, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾ (the belly of the fish would have become his grave until the Day of Resurrection). But because of his previous glorification, Allah, glorified and exalted, rescued him.

Then He said: ﴿So We threw him onto the open shore while he was sick﴾ [As-Saffat 145]. Nabdh means throwing and casting. Here He said: ﴿So We threw him﴾ in the plural form, although the one who throws is? 

* Student: The one who throws is (...).

* The Shaykh: Good, one. But He used the plural form as a mark of majesty, due to the perfection of His attributes and the abundance of His attributes; He magnified Himself.

He said: (﴿So We threw him onto the open shore﴾, i.e., We cast him out of the belly of the fish ﴿onto the open shore﴾, the surface of the earth, i.e., onto the shore, on that day, or after three or seven days, or twenty or forty days). We threw him onto the open shore. The open shore is the surface of the earth, and what is meant is the surface of the earth that has nothing shading it of trees or buildings, and it is called "ʿarāʾ" because it is bare of what covers it of trees and buildings. The fish spat him out onto the shore, so he, peace be upon him, remained on the shore with no building or trees to shade him: open. But Allah, glorified and exalted, was gentle with him, because the mercy of Allah precedes His wrath: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir 7].

He said: ﴿while he was sick﴾. As for the author's statement that it was on that day, or after three days, or four days, or seven days, or twenty days, or forty days, these are opinions, and none of them has evidence. But there is no doubt that Allah, glorified and exalted, kept him in the belly of the fish as long as Allah willed. As for specifying that, there must be evidence from one whose word is a proof, namely the Messenger (ﷺ). Anything other than that in such matters is not accepted.

He said: (﴿while he was sick﴾, weak, like a featherless chick). His saying "weak" is an explanation of "sick", and "sakam" means illness and ailment. As for his saying "like a featherless chick", meaning one whose hair has been plucked, there is nothing in the verse indicating that. But there is no doubt that the sick person is weak in body and has no capacity to withstand the sun and the wind. And His saying ﴿while he was sick﴾ indicates, on its apparent meaning, that Jonah remained in the belly of the fish for a period that led to his sickness.

He says: ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine﴾ [As-Saffat 146] (it is the squash, which shades him with its stem, contrary to the custom of squash, as a miracle for him). "We caused to grow over him", and He did not say "We caused to grow for him", because he now needed shade, so Allah caused to grow over him a shade, this tree ﴿a tree of gourd﴾. The "min" here is explanatory of kind, as one says "a ring of iron". And "yaqtin" is squash. Squash has kinds in reality: among them is a squash called here "Najdi squash", which has a tree, and its branches are soft like silk. It is said that flies do not settle on it. As for the second kind of squash, its leaves are rough, so that when a person touches it with his hand he senses roughness. The apparent meaning is that what Allah caused to grow over him was of the first kind, the soft one that is like silk, and it also gives cool shade. Allah caused this tree to grow over him. As for the author's statement that it had a stem contrary to custom, this needs evidence, but there is no doubt that Allah caused to grow over him a tree that shaded him, and it must have some height.

﴿And We sent him﴾. He said: (And a doe would come to him morning and evening, and he would drink from her milk until he grew strong). The "waʿla" is the female of the wild goats, i.e., the female of the wild goats; she would come to him and he would drink from her milk until he grew strong. This report needs evidence from an infallible source, and there is no evidence from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So it is an Israelite report about which we suspend judgment: we neither affirm nor deny it. If Allah arranged that for him, then Allah is over all things capable. This is a sensory means that a person needs; he needs food. And if Allah strengthened him to bear hunger and thirst, that is also not far-fetched, and then we would take the verse to mean that Allah strengthened him contrary to custom. But if we take it as the doe, then his survival and nourishment would be according to custom in one respect, and a miracle in another respect, according to custom: he was nourished by what? By milk, like other humans. Contrary to custom: Allah arranged for him this doe, which is not of his kind, to come so that he could drink from her milk. But if we say that Allah strengthened him to bear hunger and thirst, this becomes a pure sign, and this is not far-fetched; for when the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade continuous fasting, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are continuing." Continuous fasting means a fasting person joins two days without breaking the fast between them. They said: "You are continuing," and he said: «Indeed I am not like your state; indeed I spend the night with my Lord, who feeds me and gives me drink»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1965) and Muslim (1103/57) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], meaning without eating or drinking. And he is content with what Allah has deposited in his heart of love for Allah and remembrance of Him, instead of physical food; that is, he is content with spiritual nourishment in place of physical nourishment. Allah is over all things capable.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 37, verses 139–148 (part 2 of 3):

A similar example in some respects is that Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were in the cave, he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."﴾ [At-Tawbah 40]. Here Allah did not mention how He helped him against Quraysh while he was in the cave. So what is this to be understood as? Weak narrations have come down that a spider spun its web over him, that a dove perched at the mouth of the cave, and that Allah caused a tree to grow that blocked the sight of the polytheists from the Messenger ﷺ and his companion Abu Bakr.[[Narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad (4344), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1082), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam, al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, and Anas ibn Malik.]] These three things are sensory matters that prevent seeing the Prophet ﷺ and his companion in the cave. They are ordinary sensory matters. But is their existence at that moment a sign or not? It is a sign: that Allah caused this tree to grow and subjected this dove to stand at the entrance of the cave, and subjected the spider to weave over its door. This is undoubtedly a sign. But there is a greater sign than this, a pure sign: that Allah, exalted, blinded their eyes from seeing the Prophet ﷺ and his companion, because they stood at the cave, standing on their feet, until Abu Bakr said: "If one of them had looked at his feet, he would have seen us."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3653) and Muslim (2381/1), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.]] This is established in al-Bukhari and Muslim and others. This indicates the weakness of the story of the spider, the dove, and the tree, because the second is a clearer sign than the first. Abu Bakr's statement indicates that there was no sensory barrier preventing sight, neither a tree nor a spider's web. Nor is there anything to rule out that a dove could land at its door while someone was inside the cave, just as a dove may land at the door of a room even when someone is inside, as is frequently observed.

The conclusion is that some people bring up such signs without considering that they weaken the aspect of the sign. For the sign that Allah blinded the eyes of Quraysh from seeing the Messenger ﷺ and Abu Bakr, although they were standing right at the cave, is far greater than the spider, the tree, or the dove. Moreover, the best of these narrations in terms of chain is the spider's web narration.[[Narrated by Ahmad (3251) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] Nevertheless, it is weak. And if a narration is weak in its chain and anomalous (shadh) in its text, because it contradicts what came in the two Sahihs, it is not acceptable.

Now we return to the story of Yunus. The author mentioned that the mountain goat would come to him and he would suckle from it until he became strong. What did we say about this report? We said: this report is not established from an infallible source. Our position regarding it is to suspend judgment and say: this is not definitive, and perhaps Allah helped Yunus to endure hunger and thirst.

He (the author) said: (﴿And We sent him﴾ afterward, as before, to the people of Nineveh, in the land of Mosul in Iraq, ﴿to a hundred thousand, or more﴾ — rather, ﴿they were more﴾, twenty or thirty or seventy thousand more, ﴿and they believed﴾ at the sight of the punishment they had been promised, ﴿so We let them enjoy for a time﴾, meaning We let them remain, enjoying, ﴿for a time﴾.) Allah, exalted, sent him after that to his people, meaning He completed his mission, ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾. ﴿To a hundred thousand﴾ is explicit regarding the number. As for His saying, ﴿or more﴾, the scholars differed concerning the (or) here. It was said that it means (rather), as the author said, meaning: rather, more than a hundred thousand. As for specifying this as an increase of twenty or thirty or seventy thousand, there is no evidence for it, and the increase cannot be seventy thousand. For if the increase were seventy thousand, it would not be correct to say: ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾; rather, it would be said: "to a hundred and seventy thousand," because the difference between the first number and the second would be large. So according to the author's statement, Allah sent him to more than a hundred thousand, and (or) here would mean (rather). What is meant by it, namely by (rather) that is or has the same meaning, is the transitional idrab (change of subject, al-idrab al-intiqali, "a shift to a new point"), not the cancelling idrab (al-idrab al-ibtali, "a retraction of what came before"), because they say: idrab is either to cancel what preceded, or to move from it to what follows.

Some scholars held that (or) here is for confirmation (tahqiq) and not for idrab. That is: if they did not exceed a hundred thousand, they did not fall below it. So what follows (or) is to confirm what precedes it, not to add to it. This is like when someone asks you about your people: "How many are they?" and you say: "A hundred thousand or more," meaning that if they are not more, they are not fewer. The intention is not to affirm a majority or an increase over this number, but to confirm this number.

There is a possibility, but it does not arise in this context, that (or) is for doubt. This possibility is not valid here. Why? Because doubt can never apply to the report of Allah, given the completeness of His knowledge of everything. Accordingly, (or) here is either in the sense of (rather), or for confirmation, namely confirming the earlier number. On the first view, those sent to were more than a hundred thousand. On the second, those sent to were a hundred thousand, but this was emphasized by His saying: ﴿or more﴾.

If Allah wills, the rest of the discussion on the verse and its benefits will come later.

* Student: When Allah mentioned the story of Yunus and that he fled on the ship, he mentioned Yunus's state, then (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, in Surah Yunus Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed and whose faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [Yunus 98]. There is in this some praise of them. In reality, they had a fault on one side, and on the other side their blame is averted.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, the infallibility of the prophets (...) how is the report about Yunus, peace be upon him, here?
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: That is, he did not seek permission and went out in anger...
* Shaykh: We will discuss that in the benefits.
* Student: The author's statement that the stopping of the ship was because of Yunus, what is its basis, shaykh? Because Allah, exalted, decreed the stopping of the ship in order to make clear that Yunus was in this trial. That is, how can there be a basis for attributing it to Yunus?
* Shaykh: We should take a rule: that which goes beyond the normal course needs evidence. Otherwise, matters remain according to what is customary.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons? Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses? Is it not that they say, out of their own falsehood, 'Allah has begotten,' and they are indeed liars? Did He choose daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Will you not remember?"﴾ [As-Saffat 149–155].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers.﴾ This sentence is emphasized with how many emphases?
* Student: Two.
* Shaykh: ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers.﴾ What are they?
* Student: Inna and the lam.
* Shaykh: Inna and the lam, good. What is the wisdom in its being emphasized with two emphases? Why was it not limited to a mere statement?
* Student: Because the message may reach someone who believes, and someone who is in doubt about it, or who denies it.
* Shaykh: Because some people deny the message. That is one?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: And the second?
* Student: Because the messengers, peace be upon them, were emphasized with moral matters, so they were also emphasized...
* Shaykh: No, let us leave the ways of emphasis. And because of the importance of the establishment of his messengership, so that we believe in him. Good. His saying: ﴿when he fled to the laden ship﴾, Muhammad, ﴿when he fled﴾: (idh) here is an adverb related to what?
* Student: Related to "the messengers."
* Shaykh: To "the messengers."
* Student: Related to ﴿Remember﴾.
* Shaykh: To an omitted verb.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: (...) related to ﴿Remember﴾.
* Shaykh: Well done, correct. Because there is no basis for praising him at the time of his fleeing. His saying: ﴿So he was among those cast off﴾: the author took a course contrary to the apparent meaning. What is it?
* Student: That the people of the ship, when...
* Shaykh: No, only ﴿among those cast off﴾.
* Student: That is, he was a slave who fled from his master (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (Min) here is partitive.
* Shaykh: No. What did the author take, which we then refuted?
* Student: That he said: the people of the ship said: a slave fled from his master.
* Shaykh: No, yes.
* Student: He said that they said: Yunus was thrown into the sea because of his situation.
* Shaykh: Alone?
* Student: Alone.
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: And (min) is partitive, meaning there were others with him.
* Shaykh: Correct. The author took the view that the one who was thrown was Yunus alone, and this contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse, because the verse indicates that there was someone else with him. Good. The clause ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: what is its grammatical position (i'rab)?
* Student: The accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal).
* Shaykh: Its position is the accusative as a circumstantial clause, from the subject of "swallowed" or from the object.
* Student: From the verb, shaykh?
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: From the object.
* Shaykh: From the object. (...) Does the verse not allow it to be from the subject? The one blamed: the fish that swallowed, or Yunus who was swallowed?
* Student: Yunus.
* Shaykh: Yunus. Then it is a circumstantial clause from the object. What is the meaning of ﴿blameworthy﴾?
* Student: That is: one who comes with what he deserves blame for.
* Shaykh: One who comes with what he deserves blame for. Correct. His saying: ﴿So had he not been among those who glorify Allah﴾: (law-la) here is a particle.
* Student: Prohibition of something because of the existence of something else.
* Shaykh: Prohibition of something because of the existence of something else. What is the prohibited thing and what is the existing thing?
* Student: The prohibited thing is his remaining in the belly of the fish.
* Shaykh: His remaining in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection. And the existing thing?
* Student: The glorification.
* Shaykh: The glorification. What is the glorification that became the cause of his coming out of the belly of the fish?
* Student: His saying: "There is no god but You, glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers."
* Shaykh: His saying: "There is no god but You, glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers."

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾. (or)?
* Student: The scholars differed. Some of them said it means (rather), and some of them said...
* Shaykh: It is for idrab.
* Student: (...) rather they are more than that.
* Shaykh: That is, according to this, the ones sent to them were more than a hundred thousand. And the second view.
* Student: The second view is that it is for confirmation, meaning if they were not two hundred thousand, they do not fall below that number.
* Shaykh: They do not fall below that number, like His saying, exalted: ﴿Then your hearts became hard after that, so they were like stones or even harder in hardness.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 74].

His saying: ﴿So We let them enjoy for a time﴾. What is the meaning of "let them enjoy"?
* Student: We stopped at it.
* Shaykh: That does not contradict it. If Allah wills, we will take it now. ﴿So We let them enjoy for a time﴾ means We let them remain until a time, and this time is the time of their appointed terms which Allah decreed for them. That is, they were not destroyed by this punishment that befell them, as He, exalted, said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed and whose faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [Yunus 98].

* There are several benefits in these verses. First: the establishment of the messengership of Yunus, peace and blessings be upon him. Following from this benefit is the obligation to believe in him as a messenger. That is, it is obligatory upon us to believe that Yunus is a messenger from Allah.
* Among its benefits: praise of Yunus, from His saying: ﴿among the messengers﴾, because there is no doubt that the station of messengership is the highest station of humankind, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [An-Nisa' 69]. This is what the Muslim nation holds: that the station of messengership is superior to every other station, and is the highest station of humankind. This is contrary to those who claim that the highest station of humankind is sainthood (wilayah), then prophethood, then messengership, and who said in this a reprehensible statement, saying:
  "The station of prophethood is in an isthmus, above the Messenger and below the saint."
These people, a group among the Sufis, say: the station of prophethood is in an isthmus, above the Messenger, and below the saint, meaning far below. So sainthood is then the highest thing. They lied in this. The station of messengership is the highest of stations. Every messenger is a saint, but not vice versa. Then prophethood, then sainthood.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is not permitted to disparage Yunus because of what occurred from him of impatience. For Allah said: ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾. But it is not permitted for us to disparage him for that, because he is one of the messengers, and disparaging the messengers is disbelief. Indeed the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta."[[I have not found it with this wording. In al-Bukhari (3395) and Muslim (2377/167), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, with the wording: "No servant should say, I am better than Yunus ibn Matta."]] He forbade us to prefer him over Yunus, out of humility on his part, ﴿and so that preference (of the Messenger ﷺ) does not lead to contempt for Yunus.
* Among the benefits of the noble verses: the establishment of a group of messengers, from His saying: ﴿among the messengers﴾. But how many messengers are there? Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 24]. There is no nation among the nations but that a messenger came to it, establishing the proof against it, as Allah said: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [An-Nisa' 165].
* Among the benefits of the noble verses: that the station of prophethood does not prevent doing some things that are not beloved to Allah. That is, a messenger may commit some sins or do something he was not commanded to do. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿when he fled to the laden ship﴾. Ibaq (fleeing) means running away: a slave fleeing from his master. When a slave flees from his master, he has run away from him in rebellion against him. But there is no doubt that this description applies only to a slave owned by a human being, not to Yunus, peace and blessings be upon him. Yet Allah expressed his departure as ibaq because he departed in a manner he had not been commanded to.

This matter, namely the question of the infallibility of the messengers, is a subject of long and broad disagreement among the scholars, and we have previously explained it in detail. We mentioned that they are infallible from everything that would injure or contradict the messengership, such as lying, betrayal, shirk, and the like. They are certainly infallible from these, because they came to destroy shirk, and it is impossible that lying or betrayal should come from them, since that would lead to doubt about what they brought.

Second: they are infallible from what? 
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We mentioned it. They are also infallible from everything that undermines honour, such as theft and similar things that are regarded as baseness and vileness. This is because prophethood is the highest station of humankind, so those who are characterized by it should not adopt the most despicable morals of humankind.

The third point: they are protected from persisting in sin. They cannot be left to continue in it. Rather, they must be alerted to it, and repentance is granted to them. This differs from other people, who may commit sin and persist in it without being granted repentance. As for the claim that they have no sins at all, this view contradicts the Book and the Sunnah. God Most High said to the noblest of messengers, ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and for the believing men and believing women﴾ [Muhammad 19], and He said to him, ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath 1-2]. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, forgive me all my sins, the small and the great, the open and the secret, the first and the last. O Allah, forgive me what I have done in advance and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public" [Narrated by Muslim (483/216) from Abu Hurayrah]. All of this clearly shows that the Messenger (ﷺ) may commit a sin, but the crucial matter is that he does not persist in it.

* Among the benefits of these noble verses: Allah, glorified and exalted, may facilitate for the servant what he never expected. This is seen in His words, ﴿when he fled to the loaded ship﴾, where He decreed that he board this filled ship in order to accomplish the purpose Allah intended, which was that the fish swallow him, hide him, and confine him until it became clear to him that there is no escape from the decree of Allah. As Allah, the Exalted, said, ﴿And [mention] Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. But he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers"﴾ [al-Anbiya' 87].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of al-musahamah (drawing lots), meaning al-qur'ah (casting lots), based on His words, ﴿and he drew lots﴾.

If someone says: "This is from the law of those before us?"

The answer: the law of those before us is law for us as long as our law does not reveal something contrary to it. How much more so when our law has come in agreement with it? The Prophet (ﷺ) "used to draw lots among his wives when he intended to travel, and whichever wife's lot came out, he would take her with him" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2593) and Muslim (2445/88) from 'Aishah].

Therefore, what is derived from this is the permissibility of al-musahamah, meaning al-qur'ah.

If someone says: "Drawing lots involves risk, and it is a form of gambling (maysir), because a person may be a gainer (ghanim) or a loser (gharim)?"

The answer to this is one of two ways: either prohibition or acceptance. However, because necessity called for it, we accept it. Either we prohibit it, by saying that in a lottery a person cannot be a gainer or a loser, but is either a gainer or safe, and never loses anything; or we say that it involves uncertainty (gharar), but necessity calls for it, since distinguishing between co-owners in a right is impossible except through lots. Therefore, when distinction can be made without lots, it is obligatory to distinguish without them. For example, the Prophet's (ﷺ) drawing lots among his wives when he wished to travel: we say that he could not take all of them, because if he could, he would have taken them all. So he must distinguish who deserves to go out. How do we distinguish? We say: the last of them, the youngest of them, the eldest of them. We do not know, since they are equal in rights, and there is no way to specify except by lots. So when the lot comes out for one of them, the others have lost nothing; the only thing that happens is that they miss what they desired. For this reason, if the lot shifts from this purpose to gambling, it becomes prohibited.

An example of this: two partners in wheat wished to divide the wheat between them, and they were partners in equal shares, each owning half. They divided the wheat into thirds, meaning two-thirds were placed on one side and one-third on the other, and they wanted to draw lots as to which of them would take the two-thirds. The lot here is prohibited, because one of them is either a gainer or a loser: either he receives more than his right, or his right is reduced. This becomes prohibited because it has clearly become gambling. But if we divided the wheat into halves and wanted to distinguish each one's right, what is the way if neither yields to the other, allowing him to choose and saying, "Choose whatever you wish"? There is no way to distinguish between them except by lots.

Now, has the lot been mentioned in the Qur'an in any place other than this? Yes, in Al 'Imran: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens [to determine] which of them should be entrusted with Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ [Al 'Imran 44].

* From the benefits of the verse: there is no specific method for the lot or for al-musahamah. Whatever achieves the distinction may be used, whether by writing slips, or using stones, or rolls of cloth, or any other method. The essential point is to distinguish the one who has the right by any means, because al-musahamah is mentioned in the texts without specifying a particular method for it. So whatever method leads us to it is permissible.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: committing the lesser of two harms to avert the greater. The reasoning is that this lot would result in the destruction of some passengers, which is less severe than the destruction of all.

Therefore, if one of two harms is unavoidable, it is obligatory to commit the lesser, because committing the lesser removes from us committing the greater corruption, and avoiding the greater corruption is obligatory. For this reason we say: it is obligatory to commit the lesser of two harms to avert the greater.

These verses are evidence for acting upon such a principle. That is, if people were in a ship, and the ship was loaded, and it was necessary either to throw some passengers overboard or for all to perish, then it is permissible to throw some passengers overboard, but by way of lot, so that the rest may survive.

If someone says: "How can we throw this man into the sea to his destruction? Is this not killing a soul?" What is the answer? We take the man, knowing that he will die, and throw him into the sea. Is this not killing a soul?

We say: Yes, it is killing a soul, but to preserve souls. Which is preferable: that all be killed or that some be saved? The second is undoubtedly preferable, and this is a matter that cannot be avoided. Because if we preserved everyone, we would have caused the destruction of everyone. Causing the destruction of some is less serious than causing the destruction of all. However, this is on condition that there is no possibility, even a weak one, of rescue. If there is such a possibility, then such an act is not permissible. Now, if the ship is loaded with goods, food, sheep, and people, with whom do we begin throwing? The goods, which have no soul. If that is not enough, we throw the food. If that is not enough, we throw the animals. If that is still not enough, we cast lots among the people.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the occurrence of one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, namely that this fish was subjected to Yunus so that it swallowed him without chewing. There is no doubt that this is from the signs of Allah, because such a thing is rare according to custom. Normally, a creature chews and then swallows, but this one swallowed him whole without breaking any of his bones or crushing any part of his ribs or other parts.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the love of excuse from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He loves to be given excuses by His creatures. That is, to establish a justification for what He, Mighty and Majestic, does, so that His act is not attributed to injustice or foolishness. This is derived from His words, ﴿So the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾, meaning he was not in a state for which he would not be blamed, so that it could be said that this involved injustice to him or foolishness on His part. Rather, the fish swallowed him in a state in which he deserved that, and for this reason He said, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾.

* From the benefits of the verses: prophets may commit something for which they are blamed, but Allah facilitates their escape from it. This is based on His words, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: previous acts of obedience are a cause of deliverance from later destructions. This is based on His words, ﴿And had he not been of those who exalt [Allah], he would have remained within its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾. This provides evidence for the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Become acquainted with Allah in prosperity, and He will know you in adversity" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3382) from Abu Hurayrah, and Ahmad (2803) from Ibn 'Abbas]. This is as much the implication of verbal texts as it is of actual events. The three men in the cave, whom the cave closed upon [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2272) and Muslim (2743/99) from Ibn 'Umar], were delivered by Allah through what? Through their righteous deeds that had preceded. So when you perform a righteous deed, this deed may be a cause of your deliverance from great hardships. "Become acquainted with Allah in prosperity, and He will know you in adversity." And here He said, ﴿And had he not been of those who exalt [Allah], he would have remained within its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: if he had remained in its belly, that would have been a sign from the signs of Allah, that this fish would remain from that time until the Day of Resurrection, because this is the apparent meaning of the wording: he would remain in its belly until resurrection.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the actions of created beings are attributed to Allah, but they are attributed to Him in terms of decree and predestination, and they are attributed to the doer directly in terms of acquisition (kasb). This is derived from His words, ﴿So We threw him onto the open land﴾, since it is well known that the one who expelled him was the fish. Nevertheless, we do not affirm this definitively, because perhaps the fish expelled him and Allah facilitated for him a wind that carried him until he reached dry land. It is also possible that the fish expelled him onto dry land. Allah knows best. The essential point is that Allah facilitated for him the means of reaching dry land until He brought him to it.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: a person should never despair of recovery, even if his illness reaches its utmost extent. This is based on His words, ﴿while he was ill﴾, through to His words, ﴿and We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat 147]. This sick man who remained in the belly of the fish for as long as Allah willed came out sick, and Allah granted him health and healing. So do not despair of the mercy of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, because of the illness that befalls you. Allah may facilitate for you what becomes a cause of your recovery.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: affirming the effect of causes. This is based on His words, ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine﴾ [al-Saffat 146], because this plant shaded him and cooled him. As we have previously mentioned, it is soft to the touch, and it is said that flies do not settle on it. Allah is capable of shading him with a cloud, for example, and capable of leaving him in the sun in the open without being affected. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes clear to His servants that things occur through their causes. Yesterday, in usul al-fiqh (principles of jurisprudence), we went over the explanation that causes are effective, but not by themselves; rather, through what Allah has placed in them of the power to produce effects.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, sends earlier messengers to particular peoples. This is based on His words, ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾. Some later scholars used this verse as evidence for establishing a census of population, because He said, ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾, thus counting them numerically, even though He could have said, "We sent him to his people," which would have sufficed. Instead, He counted them. We know of no benefit for this except enumeration. There is no doubt that if enumeration has a benefit, it falls under the general texts that indicate the existence of what is beneficial. But if it has no benefit, and is merely prolonging the period, wasting time, and squandering money on what is spent upon it, then it is like anything else that has no benefit and is not sought.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, saved the people of Yunus after they witnessed the punishment. This is based on His words, ﴿Then they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾.

If someone says: "What is the wisdom in Allah singling out the people of Yunus for this, by accepting their repentance after the punishment had descended?" The answer is that the wisdom behind this is that their prophet did not remain patient until the establishment of proof against them was complete. Rather, he left them in anger before he was permitted, so the establishment of proof was not completed. Therefore, they had a kind of excuse for the delay of punishment from them.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: even if a person is saved from the destructive causes, he will not escape death. Rather, it is inevitable, whether the time is long or short. This is based on His words, ﴿so We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾.

* From its benefits: faith is a cause of a long life. This is based on His words, ﴿Then they believed, so We gave them enjoyment﴾. There is no doubt that faith is a cause of a long life, because Nuh said to his people, ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and give you respite until a specified term﴾ [Nuh 4]. So he made clear to them that if faith and repentance occurred from them, Allah would forgive them and delay them until a specified term, and if they did not do so, Allah would destroy them.

* From the benefits of all the verses: the affirmation of the greatness of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, because He attributes actions to Himself, by means of what? By the plural pronoun. It is well known that Allah is one. This has been confused for the Christians, may the curse of Allah be upon them. It became confusing for them, so they affirmed a plurality of gods because of the plural pronoun attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is following the ambiguous (mutashabih), for they followed this ambiguity and turned away from the clear statement in His words, ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 163].

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers. When he fled to the laden ship, and he drew lots and was among the losers, so the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected. So We threw him onto the open shore while he was sick, and We caused to grow over him a gourd vine, and We sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time. So ask them: Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?﴾ [As-Saffat 139–149].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers﴾. This sentence is emphasized with two emphatics: the first is (inna) and the second is the lam. The reason for the emphasis is that the establishment of prophethood is something that many people deny, and what is denied must be emphasized with what proves its establishment, whether by verbal emphasis through emphatic particles, or by semantic emphasis through mention of the signs and evidences that prove it. The prophets, peace be upon them, have had their prophethood established by both kinds; that is, by verbal emphasis and by semantic emphasis. So Allah the Exalted supported them with cosmic and legal signs, and Allah supported their message with verbal emphatics, as in this verse. He said: ﴿And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers﴾, meaning among the people whom Allah the Exalted sent to His servants. He did not specify to whom he was sent, but it is mentioned in other verses that he was sent to his people. Likewise it is authentically related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that "every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, but I have been sent to all people"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. Jonah is one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, whom Allah the Exalted sent to his people, and its explanation of his story will come, Allah willing, here. Then He said: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾.

﴿When he fled﴾. The author said: (fled ﴿to the laden ship﴾, the filled ship, when he became angry at his people), to the end. His saying ﴿when he fled﴾ may mean that (idh) is connected to "the messengers", i.e., among the messengers in this state, meaning that his fleeing did not strip him of the message. It may also be connected to an implied verb, with the sense: "Remember when he fled to the laden ship." This is better: that it is connected to an implied verb, because when He established his messengership, He mentioned one of his states, namely his fleeing, peace be upon him. Based on this, we say: ﴿when he fled﴾ is not connected to "the messengers", because his messengership was before he fled, but it is connected to an implied verb, the meaning being: remember when he fled. Al-Ibaq is fleeing, and it seems he, peace be upon him, went out hastily because he went out angry with his people when they did not believe and the punishment did not descend upon them.

He said: ﴿the laden ship﴾. The ship (al-fulk) means the vessel, which are the watercraft. Allah has blessed the servants with the ship that runs on the sea by His command, carrying provisions from one place to another, and Allah has bestowed it upon the servants as a favor, and His grace is great in our present age. The ship in our present age is not like the ship of the past. The ship of the past depended on sails and wind, had obstacles, and had great dangers. As for the ship now, it is the opposite of that. Allah has also favored His servants with ships in our present age, in that these vessels have diversified: they have become a water vessel, a land vessel, and an air vessel. The air vessel is the aircraft, the land is vehicles, and the water is ships, and all of this falls under His saying the Exalted: ﴿And He has made for you of ships and livestock that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them, and say: Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 12–13].

And His saying: ﴿the laden ship﴾. The author said: (the filled ship), meaning ﴿the laden﴾ in the sense of filled with passengers. So he boarded the sea (angry with his people, when the punishment he had promised them did not descend upon them, so he boarded the ship, and it stopped in the depths of the sea. The sailors said: here is a slave who has fled from his master; the lot will reveal him). Thus said the author, may Allah have mercy on him: that the ship stopped in the depths of the sea, and its stopping was because of Jonah's fleeing. The sailors said, and they were the ship's captains: here is a slave who has fled from his master; the lot will reveal him. However, what the author mentioned has no evidence for it, and it is one of the distant Israelite narrations. Rather, when this laden ship was in the open sea, and it was laden and filled, and it reached the depths of the sea, the load became heavy. When the load becomes heavy, one of two things must happen: either the load is lightened, or everyone drowns. There is no doubt that lightening the load is preferable to everyone drowning, because if the load is lightened, those who remain are saved, and if the load remains as it is, everyone drowns. The survival of some is preferable to the destruction of all. This is a matter of reason. They drew lots, meaning it was not preferable to cast some of them into the sea rather than others, so there was no way to escape this problem except by lot. So they drew lots.

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾ [As-Saffat 141]. They drew lots as to who would be cast out. It is known that when we know who will be cast out, we know who will remain. For this reason Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Sahama means (he cast lots with the people of the ship). ﴿And was among the losers﴾ (those overcome by the lot, so they cast him into the sea). The apparent sense of the author's presentation, may Allah have mercy on him, is that no one was cast out except Jonah. But the verse indicates otherwise than what the author's words indicate, because His saying ﴿and was among the losers﴾, here the (min) is partitive, meaning: one of them. This indicates that the lot fell upon him and also fell upon others. So the matter is now clear: the ship was laden, and the ship must sink unless some of its passengers are cast out. Casting out some passengers is preferable to the destruction of all. There is no way to cast out some by specific designation, because if we designated one person over another, that would be injustice, and the one designated would refuse, and it would become a dispute, and perhaps the ship would sink in the midst of this dispute. So what is the way to designate who is cast out? It is the lot.

So they drew lots, and the lot fell upon some people, and some people were saved from it, and Jonah was among those whom the lot fell upon: ﴿and was among the losers﴾, so he was cast into the sea.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿Then the fish swallowed him﴾, it swallowed him, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, meaning: he did what he was to be blamed for, by going to the sea and boarding the ship without permission from his Lord). The fish swallowed him in one piece, and did not chew him, because if it had chewed him he would have been broken and perished. But Allah subjected this fish to him, so it swallowed him whole and gulped him down, until he reached the place of its belly without any harm befalling him. As for His saying ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, the clause here is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in His saying (swallowed him), not from the subject of (swallowed). Because the subject is who? The fish, and the fish is not blameworthy. The blameworthy one is the one swallowed.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾, meaning Jonah. The meaning of ﴿blameworthy﴾ is one who does what he is to be blamed for, just as one says "munajjid" for someone who has entered Najd, for example. So mufʿil may come to mean being characterized by something. The blameworthy one is the one who did what he deserved blame for. And what is he blamed for? That he left his people angry with them before Allah had given him permission, and it was obligatory for him to be patient. For this reason Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was suppressing grief. Had not a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast out onto the open shore while he was blameworthy. But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾ [Al-Qalam 48–50]. The point is that Jonah, peace be upon him, was swallowed by the fish in a state for which he was blameworthy. What is the basis of that? What is the basis of that?

* Student: That he went out angry from his people without permission from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [As-Saffat 142–144]. (Lawla) occurs often in the Qur'an, in the Sunnah, and in people's speech, so what is it? I say: (lawla) comes in several senses. First: it is a particle of prohibition due to existence, meaning its consequent is prevented because its condition exists: (Lawla Allah ma ihtadayna), the non-guidance is negated because of Allah's existence.
